newsitem.title: USA: Most ValuJet cases to be heard in Fla. state court.
newsitem.headline: Most ValuJet cases to be heard in Fla. state court.

text.p: A federal judge ruled Tuesday that most of the wrongful death cases filed against ValuJet and its maintenance contractor following the Flight 592 crash should be heard in state court, a plaintiff's attorney said.

U.S. District Judge Edward Davis ruled in favour of victims' relatives who said their claims against ValuJet and SabreTech for damages resulting from the loss of loved ones should not be heard in federal courts, Aaron Podhurst, a lawyer representing some of the families, said.

Flight 592 crashed in Florida's Everglades on May 11, killing all 110 passengers and crew on board. A public hearing into the crash last week elicited testimony that dozens of oxygen canisters improperly packed and labeled by SabreTech may have started or fuelled a fire in the DC-9's cargo hold. Determination of an official cause is still months away.

Lawyers for the families argued that the federal court system did not have jurisdiction over the wrongful death lawsuits because the cases hinged on negligence. Podhurst said at least 30 pending cases would be heard in Florida state courts while only a handful would be tried in federal court.
A few cases have been filed in Georgia, where ValuJet is headquartered.

He said trial of the cases in federal court could have resulted in years of wasted time if higher courts then ruled that the federal court was not the proper venue. "That would have been a tragedy," he said.
A lawyer for ValuJet argued that because the lawsuits hinged on air safety -- regulated by the federal government -- the lawsuits belonged in federal court.
